Senses.PreferredTarget: one horse gives birth to three tigers
AlternateTargets: one mare produces three tiger cubs
Senses.Note: Four independent masters preserve the same impossible animal birth in hall answers and capping lines.

Occurrences.Kwic: 眾舉首，師云：「鐵蛇橫古路，一馬生三寅。參！」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB288.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hanyu Xian. Hanyu Hongxian presses the assembly down with his staff, then pairs an iron snake across the old road with one horse producing three tigers and commands investigation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又喝一喝，云：「一馬生三寅。」又喝一喝，云：「此中一句，能令山河大地、草木風雲、情與無情一時轉大法輪、成等正覺。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB299.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Sanfeng Zang. Hanyue Fazang gives the animal-birth line between two shouts and then calls it the line at issue.

Occurrences.Kwic: 忽然一馬生三寅，便道：見怪不怪，其怪自壞。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB362.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guantaoqi. Guantao Daqi introduces the horse-and-three-tigers line with ‘suddenly’ and follows it with the saying that a marvel ceases to be strange when one does not regard it as strange.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「假饒百千文殊亦出此女子定不得，未審世尊恁麼道，是好心？不是好心？」師云：「一馬生三寅。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB383.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hanxiu. Hanxiu Ruqian answers a monk’s question about the woman’s absorption case with one horse giving birth to three tigers.

Senses.Explanation: One horse gives birth to three tigers pictures an impossible crossing of animal kinds and numbers. Chan masters preserve the image intact as a hall cap and direct answer, often beside another impossible creature or a remark about marvels. Hanyu pairs it with an iron snake across the old road; Hanyue isolates it between shouts; Guantao places it before ‘regard no marvel as strange’; and Hanxiu answers a question about the woman-in-absorption case with it.
